title: Resume an upload the network cut off
description:
**Ask:** Resume an upload after the network drops, instead of losing every byte already sent.

## Why (Computational)

`upload/store.py` writes one whole photo per request. A dropped network loses the bytes
already sent, so the person uploads the same photo again.

## Estimated size

2 files, 60 LOC, band: Target.
design:
Write each chunk to a part file under `upload/parts/`, then join the parts when the last
chunk arrives.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Given a dropped network, when the person uploads the same photo again, then only the
   missing chunks are sent.
notes:
## Done when (Acceptance)

- A resumed upload sends only the missing chunks.

title: Add a second test for the thumbnail width
description:
**Ask:** Add one more test that checks the width of a thumbnail.

## Why (Computational)

`tests/test_thumbnail.py` already checks the thumbnail width. A second test would check the
same width a second way.

## Estimated size

1 file, 20 LOC, band: Small.
design: Add one test beside the test at `tests/test_thumbnail.py`.
acceptance_criteria: 1. Given a wide photo, when the thumbnail is built, then its width is 320 pixels.
notes:
## Done when (Acceptance)

- A second test checks the thumbnail width.

title: Let a viewer sort an album by camera model
description:
**Ask:** Let a viewer sort an album by the camera that took each photo.

## Why (Computational)

`album/view.py` sorts an album by date and offers no other order. Nobody has asked for
another order.

## Estimated size

2 files, 80 LOC, band: Target.
design: Read the camera model out of the photo metadata, then add a sort option to `album/view.py`.
acceptance_criteria: 1. Given an album, when the viewer picks camera order, then the photos sort by camera model.
notes:
## Done when (Acceptance)

- An album sorts by camera model.
